target.statement: Mean AUC-PR of Online methods vs Streaming methods on TSB-AD-M (full training size): Online 0.2807 vs Streaming 0.1713, +63.91% relative gain
target.dataset: TSB-AD-M (200 multivariate real-world time series, 17 datasets)

compute.basis: Reproducing the mean over 200 series requires running 19 static/online methods (incl. deep models like TranAD, TimesNet, AnomalyTransformer, OmniAnomaly) plus 10 streaming methods in Java/C++/Python across 17 datasets, with hyperparameter grids already tuned; even a single-cell mean needs the full benchmark sweep, and the deep baselines are the dominant cost.

blockers: Target is an aggregate over 200 series and ~29 methods, not a single cheap cell
Requires building/running Java (MCOD, LEAP), C++ (dSalmon: xStream, SWKNN, SDOstream) and Python (pysad, TSB-AD) stacks
Deep-learning baselines (TranAD, TimesNet, AnomalyTransformer, OmniAnomaly, USAD) are heavy to train/infer on CPU
TSB-AD-M data must be downloaded and preprocessed; some datasets (SWaT, Exathlon) may have access restrictions
title: In a Streaming World, Should You Stand Still? A Comprehensive Benchmark of Anomaly Detection in Streams
